# wallix-bastion_passwordchangepolicy (Data Source)

Get information on a password change policy, including the generated password's shape (length,
character classes), the SSH key parameters used instead of a password, and the rotation schedule.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Get information about a specific password change policy
data "wallix-bastion_passwordchangepolicy" "strong" {
  password_change_policy_name = "strong-rotation"
}

# Reference the policy when configuring a domain
resource "wallix-bastion_domain" "corporate" {
  domain_name             = "corp.local"
  domain_real_name        = "corp.local"
  password_change_policy  = data.wallix-bastion_passwordchangepolicy.strong.password_change_policy_name
}

# Report the effective minimum password length
output "minimum_password_length" {
  value = data.wallix-bastion_passwordchangepolicy.strong.password_length
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `password_change_policy_name` (String)

### Read-Only

- `change_period` (String)
- `description` (String)
- `digit_chars` (Number)
- `exclude_chars` (String)
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `lower_chars` (Number)
- `password_length` (Number)
- `special_chars` (Number)
- `ssh_key_size` (Number)
- `ssh_key_type` (String)
- `upper_chars` (Number)

## Usage Notes

### `password_change_policy_name`

The Required lookup key. It must match an existing password change policy exactly; the data
source fails with an error if no policy with that name exists.

### Character class fields (`special_chars`, `lower_chars`, `upper_chars`, `digit_chars`)

These report the currently configured minimums for each character class in generated passwords.
On the resource side these fields carry three distinct states (unset/disallowed, `0`/allowed with
no minimum, `N`/at least `N` required); the data source simply surfaces whatever integer value the
Bastion currently reports for each class, so a value of `0` here does not distinguish between
"unset" and "explicitly allowed with no minimum" on the API side.

### SSH key rotation

If the policy rotates an SSH key instead of a password, `ssh_key_type` and `ssh_key_size` report
the configured key type and size.

### `change_period`

The cron expression (or alias such as `@weekly`) controlling how often the password/key is
rotated. Empty when no schedule is configured.
